feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 1 (16 mm footprints, 0.5 kg, 0.10 m track, kp 3.0, kd 0.15) had every trial end off-track: oval progress 0.46, max_error 0.0668, steering_oscillation 0.274, control_effort 10.7; s-bend and slalom progress 0.16 and 0.10, max_error about 0.061. The oscillation jump on the oval, against 0.075 in iteration 0, shows that narrowing the track and lowering mass raised turn response enough to make the robot underdamped. Your choice of body_length and wheel_track is the right direction for that, and the Integrator has reduced kp and raised kd to match. The next race decides the next step. If oval max_error is below 0.06 and oscillation falls, keep the geometry and treat the remaining s-bend and slalom exits as a bend-entry problem. If max_error stays near 0.06 with low oscillation, turn authority is the limit and the sensor row should move forward. If line_loss_events rise above one per run, the 16 mm footprints are overlapping too much on the outer sensors.
requested_changes: If oval max_error stays at or above 0.06 while steering_oscillation is below 0.2: move the sensor row forward from y = 0.04 to y = 0.06 (keep x and sensor_size) so the signal reacts before the wheels reach the bend. Evidence: iteration 1 oval max_error 0.0668 with oscillation 0.274 showed the excursion was not caused by lack of damping alone.

If steering_oscillation on the oval stays above 0.2 after the controller change: reduce wheel_track toward 0.10 m is wrong direction, so instead keep wheel_track at 0.09 m and raise body_length to 0.22 m for more yaw inertia. Evidence: iteration 1 oscillation rose from 0.075 to 0.274 when wheel_track and mass were reduced.

If line_loss_events rise above 1.0 per run on any track, return sensor_size to 0.012 and widen the outer sensors to x = plus or minus 0.05 m. Evidence: iteration 1 used 16 mm footprints and line_loss stayed at exactly 1.0, so the footprints are not yet causing loss, but a rise would indicate overlap near centre.
